Seasonal adjustment of tsibbles with fable.rjd3

Source: vignettes/vignette.Rmd
vignette.Rmd

Introduction

fable.rjd3 lets you seasonally adjust tsibble series with the JDemetra+ v3 algorithms, using the fabletools modelling framework. Four models are available:

Model Algorithm Decomposition
X13() X-13ARIMA (rjd3x13::jx13()) yes
TRAMOSEATS() TRAMO-SEATS (rjd3tramoseats::jtramoseats()) yes
REGARIMA() Reg-ARIMA pre-adjustment only (rjd3x13::jregarima()) no
TRAMO() TRAMO pre-adjustment only (rjd3tramoseats::jtramo()) no

The fitted models keep the underlying Java object. The usual decomposition is available through components(), and any other JDemetra+ indicator (outliers, regression coefficients, diagnostics…) can be extracted with jd3_indicator().

The package re-exports the main verbs of fabletools (model(), components(), forecast(), glance(), tidy(), report()…) and a few functions of tsibble, so that library(fable.rjd3) is enough.

library(fable.rjd3)

Quick start

The series must be a univariate tsibble with a yearmonth or yearquarter index and no gaps. The frequency is deduced from the interval between the observations, so monthly, bimonthly, quarterly, four-monthly and semi-annual series are all supported (for example, a yearmonth index with a step of 2 months is a bimonthly series, with a step of 6 months a semi-annual one). Here we use the classic AirPassengers data.

air <- as_tsibble(AirPassengers)
air
#> # A tsibble: 144 x 2 [1M]
#>       index value
#>       <mth> <dbl>
#>  1 1949 Jan   112
#>  2 1949 Feb   118
#>  3 1949 Mar   132
#>  4 1949 Apr   129
#>  5 1949 May   121
#>  6 1949 Jun   135
#>  7 1949 Jul   148
#>  8 1949 Aug   148
#>  9 1949 Sep   136
#> 10 1949 Oct   119
#> # ℹ 134 more rows

Models are fitted with model(), exactly as with other fable models. Several models can be fitted at once, which makes it easy to compare the two methods.

mb <- model(
    air,
    x13 = X13(value),
    ts  = TRAMOSEATS(value)
)
mb
#> # A mable: 1 x 2
#>                                x13                                 ts
#>                            <model>                            <model>
#> 1 <X-13ARIMA, ARIMA(0,1,1)(0,1,1)> <TRAMO-SEATS, ARIMA(0,1,0)(0,1,1)>

The model summary shows the method and the selected ARIMA model.

Decomposition

For X13() and TRAMOSEATS(), components() returns a dable with the original series and the columns trend, seasonal, irregular and season_adjust. The relation between the components follows the decomposition mode of the model (additive, multiplicative, log-additive or pseudo-additive).

components(mb)
#> # A dable: 288 x 7 [1M]
#> # Key:     .model [2]
#> # :        value = trend * seasonal * irregular
#>    .model    index value trend seasonal irregular season_adjust
#>    <chr>     <mth> <dbl> <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>         <dbl>
#>  1 x13    1949 Jan   112  122.    0.920     0.996          122.
#>  2 x13    1949 Feb   118  124.    0.948     1.00           125.
#>  3 x13    1949 Mar   132  126.    1.05      0.994          125.
#>  4 x13    1949 Apr   129  128.    1.00      1.01           129.
#>  5 x13    1949 May   121  128.    0.939     1.01           129.
#>  6 x13    1949 Jun   135  127.    1.07      0.998          127.
#>  7 x13    1949 Jul   148  126.    1.19      0.988          125.
#>  8 x13    1949 Aug   148  126.    1.17      0.999          126.
#>  9 x13    1949 Sep   136  127.    1.07      1.00           128.
#> 10 x13    1949 Oct   119  128.    0.925     1.00           129.
#> # ℹ 278 more rows

With the ggtime package, the decomposition can be plotted with autoplot().

library(ggtime)
ggplot2::autoplot(components(mb))

Setting the specification

The specification can be defined in two ways, which can be combined.

Ex ante, with the spec argument

spec accepts a name (such as "rsa3" for X13() or "rsafull" for TRAMOSEATS()), or a specification object created with rjd3x13::x13_spec() / rjd3tramoseats::tramoseats_spec() and modified with the set_*() functions of rjd3toolkit. This gives access to everything JDemetra+ offers.

my_spec <- rjd3x13::x13_spec("rsa3")
my_spec <- rjd3toolkit::set_transform(my_spec, fun = "Log")
my_spec <- rjd3toolkit::add_outlier(my_spec, type = "AO", date = "1955-01-01")

mb_spec <- model(air, x13 = X13(value, spec = my_spec))
glance(mb_spec)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 19
#>   .model  aicc  nobs nparams  nout lb_stat lb_pvalue normality_stat
#>   <chr>  <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl>     <dbl>          <dbl>
#> 1 x13     989.   144       4     1    24.3     0.333           3.81
#> # ℹ 11 more variables: normality_pvalue <dbl>, ftest_sa_stat <dbl>,
#> #   ftest_sa_pvalue <dbl>, qs_test_sa_stat <dbl>, qs_test_sa_pvalue <dbl>,
#> #   combined_test_sa <chr>, combined_test_sa_lastyears <chr>,
#> #   td_on_sa_stat <dbl>, td_on_sa_pvalue <dbl>, Q <dbl>, Q_M2 <dbl>

In the formula, with specials

Specials are used on the right-hand side of the formula. Each one records a call to a function of rjd3toolkit (or of the algorithm package) that is applied to the base specification:

Special Calls
spec(x) base specification, same as the spec argument
basic(...) rjd3toolkit::set_basic()
transform(...) rjd3toolkit::set_transform()
estimate(...) rjd3toolkit::set_estimate()
automodel(...) rjd3toolkit::set_automodel()
outlier(...) rjd3toolkit::set_outlier()
add_outlier(...) rjd3toolkit::add_outlier()
easter(...) rjd3toolkit::set_easter()
tradingdays(...) rjd3toolkit::set_tradingdays()
arima(...) rjd3toolkit::set_arima()
ramp(...) rjd3toolkit::add_ramp()
usrdefvar(...) rjd3toolkit::add_usrdefvar()
benchmarking(...) rjd3toolkit::set_benchmarking() (X13() and TRAMOSEATS())
x11(...) rjd3x13::set_x11() (X13() only)
seats(...) rjd3tramoseats::set_seats() (TRAMOSEATS() only)
xreg(...) user regressors taken from tsibble columns 
mb_sp <- model(
    air,
    x13 = X13(
        value ~ transform(fun = "Log") +
            outlier(outliers.type = c("AO", "LS")) +
            x11(seasonal.filter = "S3X5")
    )
)
glance(mb_sp)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 19
#>   .model  aicc  nobs nparams  nout lb_stat lb_pvalue normality_stat
#>   <chr>  <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl>     <dbl>          <dbl>
#> 1 x13     947.   144       6     1    23.9     0.354          0.763
#> # ℹ 11 more variables: normality_pvalue <dbl>, ftest_sa_stat <dbl>,
#> #   ftest_sa_pvalue <dbl>, qs_test_sa_stat <dbl>, qs_test_sa_pvalue <dbl>,
#> #   combined_test_sa <chr>, combined_test_sa_lastyears <chr>,
#> #   td_on_sa_stat <dbl>, td_on_sa_pvalue <dbl>, Q <dbl>, Q_M2 <dbl>

The base spec is applied first, then the specials in a fixed order, then xreg(): later settings override earlier ones. A special that does not apply to the method (for example x11() in TRAMOSEATS()) is ignored with a warning.

The base specification is also stored in the model as the reference specification (argument ref_spec, by default equal to spec). It is the reference used by the refresh policies of refit() and stream(), see below.

Regressors from the tsibble

Since a specification created ex ante cannot refer to columns of your data, regressors are declared with the xreg() special. The variables are added to the modelling context, and to the specification when regeffect is given.

air$shock <- as.numeric(air$index == yearmonth("1955 Jan"))

mb_xreg <- model(air, x13 = X13(value ~ xreg(shock, regeffect = "Series")))
#> Warning: 1 error encountered for x13
#> [1] unused argument (effect = x$regeffect)
tidy(mb_xreg)
#> # A tibble: 0 × 3
#> # ℹ 3 variables: .model <chr>, term <chr>, estimate <dbl>

For custom calendars, build a context with rjd3toolkit::modelling_context() and pass it through the context argument.

Extracting results

Diagnostics and regression terms

  • glance() returns a one-row summary per model: information criteria, number of observations and outliers, tests on the residuals and, for seasonal adjustment models, tests on the seasonally adjusted series and the quality statistics of the method. Tests give two columns (_stat and _pvalue) and the combined seasonality tests give a text. The set of indicators depends on the method; glance(x, ids = ) takes a vector of indicator ids to choose others.
  • tidy() returns one row per coefficient (ARIMA parameters, regression variables, outliers, calendar effects) with its standard error, statistic and p-value. Coefficients fixed in the specification are included.
  • report() prints a summary of one model: the coefficients and the tests, in the spirit of summary() for a regression.
glance(mb)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 22
#>   .model  aicc  nobs nparams  nout lb_stat lb_pvalue normality_stat
#>   <chr>  <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl>     <dbl>          <dbl>
#> 1 x13     947.   144       6     1    23.9     0.354          0.763
#> 2 ts      936.   144       7     2    30.8     0.128          0.834
#> # ℹ 14 more variables: normality_pvalue <dbl>, ftest_sa_stat <dbl>,
#> #   ftest_sa_pvalue <dbl>, qs_test_sa_stat <dbl>, qs_test_sa_pvalue <dbl>,
#> #   combined_test_sa <chr>, combined_test_sa_lastyears <chr>,
#> #   td_on_sa_stat <dbl>, td_on_sa_pvalue <dbl>, Q <dbl>, Q_M2 <dbl>,
#> #   seas_var <dbl>, irr_var <dbl>, seas_irr_corr <dbl>
tidy(mb_sp)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 6
#>   .model term         estimate std.error statistic  p.value
#>   <chr>  <chr>           <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 x13    theta(1)     -0.116    0.109        -1.06 2.89e- 1
#> 2 x13    btheta(1)    -0.497    0.0723       -6.88 2.55e-10
#> 3 x13    td2          -0.00295  0.000533     -5.53 1.79e- 7
#> 4 x13    easter [1]    0.0178   0.00730       2.43 1.63e- 2
#> 5 x13    AO (1951-05)  0.100    0.0208        4.81 4.33e- 6
report(mb["x13"])
#> Series: value

#> 
#> 
#> Coefficients
#>                Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
#> theta(1)     -0.1155344  0.1085487  -1.064   0.2892    
#> btheta(1)    -0.4974142  0.0722919  -6.881 2.55e-10 ***
#> td2          -0.0029497  0.0005334  -5.530 1.79e-07 ***

Outliers

outliers() returns the rows of the data identified as outliers (additive outliers, level shifts, transitory changes, seasonal outliers) by the pre-adjustment model. The type argument keeps some types only, and the type and the statistics of each outlier are available in tidy().

outliers(mb)
#> # A tsibble: 3 x 3 [1M]
#> # Key:       .model [2]
#>   .model    index value
#>   <chr>     <mth> <dbl>
#> 1 x13    1951 May   172
#> 2 ts     1951 May   172
#> 3 ts     1954 Feb   188
outliers(mb, type = "AO")
#> # A tsibble: 3 x 3 [1M]
#> # Key:       .model [2]
#>   .model    index value
#>   <chr>     <mth> <dbl>
#> 1 x13    1951 May   172
#> 2 ts     1951 May   172
#> 3 ts     1954 Feb   188

Any JDemetra+ indicator

jd3_dictionary() lists the indicators available for a model, and jd3_indicator() extracts one of them via rjd3toolkit::result().

head(jd3_dictionary(mb), 15)
#>  [1] "out_i"      "out_i_f(?)" "out_i_b(?)" "out_t"      "out_t_f(?)"
#>  [6] "out_t_b(?)" "out_s"      "out_s_f(?)" "out_s_b(?)" "reg_i"     
#> [11] "reg_i_f(?)" "reg_i_b(?)" "reg_t"      "reg_t_f(?)" "reg_t_b(?)"

# the raw object, for a single model
jd3_indicator(mb$x13[[1]], "sa")

For a mable, the result depends on the type of the indicator: a number gives a column value, a series is returned in long format (index and value), and a test gives the columns statistic, p.value and distribution. With several ids, a named list is returned.

jd3_indicator(mb, "residuals.lb")
#> # A tibble: 2 × 5
#>   .model id           statistic p.value distribution                        
#>   <chr>  <chr>            <dbl>   <dbl> <chr>                               
#> 1 x13    residuals.lb      23.9   0.354 "Chi2 with 22.0 degrees of freedom "
#> 2 ts     residuals.lb      30.8   0.128 "Chi2 with 23.0 degrees of freedom "
jd3_indicator(mb, c("likelihood.aicc", "likelihood.nobs"))
#> $likelihood.aicc
#> # A tibble: 2 × 3
#>   .model id              value
#>   <chr>  <chr>           <dbl>
#> 1 x13    likelihood.aicc  947.
#> 2 ts     likelihood.aicc  936.
#> 
#> $likelihood.nobs
#> # A tibble: 2 × 3
#>   .model id              value
#>   <chr>  <chr>           <dbl>
#> 1 x13    likelihood.nobs   144
#> 2 ts     likelihood.nobs   144

Pre-adjustment models and forecasts

REGARIMA() and TRAMO() fit the pre-adjustment model only, with the same specifications and specials as X13() and TRAMOSEATS(). They have no decomposition, so no components(), but all the other methods work.

mb_pre <- model(air, regarima = REGARIMA(value), tramo = TRAMO(value))
glance(mb_pre)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 11
#>   .model    aicc  nobs nparams  nout lb_stat lb_pvalue normality_stat
#>   <chr>    <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl>     <dbl>          <dbl>
#> 1 regarima  947.   144       6     1    23.9     0.354          0.763
#> 2 tramo     936.   144       7     2    30.8     0.128          0.834
#> # ℹ 3 more variables: normality_pvalue <dbl>, lb2_stat <dbl>, lb2_pvalue <dbl>

Forecasts and backcasts

forecast() forecasts the raw series from the pre-adjustment model, for the four models. The result is a distribution: log-normal if the series is log-transformed, normal otherwise. The default point forecast .mean is the mean of the distribution; use point_forecast to choose another summary, for example the median, which is the forecast given by JDemetra+.

forecast(mb_pre, h = 12)
#> # A fable: 24 x 4 [1M]
#> # Key:     .model [2]
#>    .model      index
#>    <chr>       <mth>
#>  1 regarima 1961 Jan
#>  2 regarima 1961 Feb
#>  3 regarima 1961 Mar
#>  4 regarima 1961 Apr
#>  5 regarima 1961 May
#>  6 regarima 1961 Jun
#>  7 regarima 1961 Jul
#>  8 regarima 1961 Aug
#>  9 regarima 1961 Sep
#> 10 regarima 1961 Oct
#> # ℹ 14 more rows
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: value <dist>, .mean <dbl>
forecast(mb_pre, h = 12, point_forecast = list(.median = median))
#> # A fable: 24 x 4 [1M]
#> # Key:     .model [2]
#>    .model      index
#>    <chr>       <mth>
#>  1 regarima 1961 Jan
#>  2 regarima 1961 Feb
#>  3 regarima 1961 Mar
#>  4 regarima 1961 Apr
#>  5 regarima 1961 May
#>  6 regarima 1961 Jun
#>  7 regarima 1961 Jul
#>  8 regarima 1961 Aug
#>  9 regarima 1961 Sep
#> 10 regarima 1961 Oct
#> # ℹ 14 more rows
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: value <dist>, .median <dbl>

backcast() does the same for the periods preceding the series.

backcast(mb, h = 12)
#> # A tibble: 24 × 3
#>    .model    index
#>    <chr>     <mth>
#>  1 x13    1948 Jan
#>  2 x13    1948 Feb
#>  3 x13    1948 Mar
#>  4 x13    1948 Apr
#>  5 x13    1948 May
#>  6 x13    1948 Jun
#>  7 x13    1948 Jul
#>  8 x13    1948 Aug
#>  9 x13    1948 Sep
#> 10 x13    1948 Oct
#> # ℹ 14 more rows
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: dist <dist>

Fitted values, residuals and missing values

fitted() and residuals() give the one-step-ahead fitted values and the residuals of the pre-adjustment model, with NA where they are not defined. They make augment() and accuracy() work.

residuals(mb)
#> # A tsibble: 288 x 3 [1M]
#> # Key:       .model [2]
#>    .model    index .resid
#>    <chr>     <mth>  <dbl>
#>  1 x13    1949 Jan     NA
#>  2 x13    1949 Feb     NA
#>  3 x13    1949 Mar     NA
#>  4 x13    1949 Apr     NA
#>  5 x13    1949 May     NA
#>  6 x13    1949 Jun     NA
#>  7 x13    1949 Jul     NA
#>  8 x13    1949 Aug     NA
#>  9 x13    1949 Sep     NA
#> 10 x13    1949 Oct     NA
#> # ℹ 278 more rows
augment(mb)
#> # A tsibble: 288 x 6 [1M]
#> # Key:       .model [2]
#>    .model    index value .fitted .resid .innov
#>    <chr>     <mth> <dbl>   <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>
#>  1 x13    1949 Jan   112      NA     NA     NA
#>  2 x13    1949 Feb   118      NA     NA     NA
#>  3 x13    1949 Mar   132      NA     NA     NA
#>  4 x13    1949 Apr   129      NA     NA     NA
#>  5 x13    1949 May   121      NA     NA     NA
#>  6 x13    1949 Jun   135      NA     NA     NA
#>  7 x13    1949 Jul   148      NA     NA     NA
#>  8 x13    1949 Aug   148      NA     NA     NA
#>  9 x13    1949 Sep   136      NA     NA     NA
#> 10 x13    1949 Oct   119      NA     NA     NA
#> # ℹ 278 more rows

interpolate() replaces the missing values of the series by the estimates of the model.

air_na <- air
air_na$value[c(20, 21)] <- NA
mb_na <- model(air_na, x13 = X13(value))
interpolate(mb_na, air_na)
#> # A tsibble: 144 x 2 [1M]
#>       index value
#>       <mth> <dbl>
#>  1 1949 Jan   112
#>  2 1949 Feb   118
#>  3 1949 Mar   132
#>  4 1949 Apr   129
#>  5 1949 May   121
#>  6 1949 Jun   135
#>  7 1949 Jul   148
#>  8 1949 Aug   148
#>  9 1949 Sep   136
#> 10 1949 Oct   119
#> # ℹ 134 more rows

Updating models

When new observations arrive, a model can be updated with the refresh policies of JDemetra+ ("Fixed" by default: the estimated parameters are kept; the other policies are "FreeParameters", "Complete", "Outliers_StochasticComponent", "Outliers", "FixedParameters", "FixedAutoRegressiveParameters" and "Current"). The refresh is based on the estimated specification and on the reference specification stored in the model.

  • stream() appends the new observations to the data of the model;
  • refit() applies the model to a new complete dataset.
start_new <- yearmonth("1960 Jan")
air_old <- air[air$index < start_new, c("index", "value")]
air_new <- air[air$index >= start_new, c("index", "value")]
mb_old  <- model(air_old, x13 = X13(value))

mb_ext <- stream(mb_old, air_new)
components(mb_ext)
#> # A dable: 144 x 7 [1M]
#> # Key:     .model [1]
#> # :        value = trend * seasonal * irregular
#>    .model    index value trend seasonal irregular season_adjust
#>    <chr>     <mth> <dbl> <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>         <dbl>
#>  1 x13    1949 Jan   112  122.    0.919     0.995          122.
#>  2 x13    1949 Feb   118  125.    0.949     0.998          124.
#>  3 x13    1949 Mar   132  127.    1.05      0.997          126.
#>  4 x13    1949 Apr   129  128.    0.996     1.01           130.
#>  5 x13    1949 May   121  128.    0.943     1.00           128.
#>  6 x13    1949 Jun   135  127.    1.07      0.999          127.
#>  7 x13    1949 Jul   148  126.    1.19      0.989          125.
#>  8 x13    1949 Aug   148  126.    1.17      0.999          126.
#>  9 x13    1949 Sep   136  127.    1.07      1.00           128.
#> 10 x13    1949 Oct   119  128.    0.925     1.01           129.
#> # ℹ 134 more rows

mb_refit <- refit(mb_old, air[c("index", "value")], policy = "FreeParameters")

Several series

Because models are defined through fabletools, keyed tsibbles work as usual: one model is fitted per series.

a <- as.data.frame(air[c("index", "value")]); a$series <- "A"
b <- a; b$value <- sqrt(b$value) * 10; b$series <- "B"
two <- as_tsibble(rbind(a, b), index = index, key = series)

mb2 <- model(two, x13 = X13(value))
mb2
#> # A mable: 2 x 2
#> # Key:     series [2]
#>   series                              x13
#>   <chr>                           <model>
#> 1 A      <X-13ARIMA, ARIMA(0,1,1)(0,1,1)>
#> 2 B      <X-13ARIMA, ARIMA(0,1,0)(0,1,1)>
glance(mb2)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 20
#>   series .model  aicc  nobs nparams  nout lb_stat lb_pvalue normality_stat
#>   <chr>  <chr>  <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl>     <dbl>          <dbl>
#> 1 A      x13     947.   144       6     1    23.9     0.354          0.763
#> 2 B      x13     635.   144       5     1    26.7     0.269          0.531
#> # ℹ 11 more variables: normality_pvalue <dbl>, ftest_sa_stat <dbl>,
#> #   ftest_sa_pvalue <dbl>, qs_test_sa_stat <dbl>, qs_test_sa_pvalue <dbl>,
#> #   combined_test_sa <chr>, combined_test_sa_lastyears <chr>,
#> #   td_on_sa_stat <dbl>, td_on_sa_pvalue <dbl>, Q <dbl>, Q_M2 <dbl>

JDemetra+ workspaces

import_jws() reads a JDemetra+ workspace and fits its SA-items with the specifications it contains. The result is a mable with two keys, sap (the SA-processing) and series (the SA-item), and a model column sa. The estimation specification of the item is the specification of the model, its reference specification is kept for the refresh policies, and the modelling context of the workspace (calendars and user-defined variables) is shared by all the models.

file <- system.file("workspaces", "workspace_test.xml", package = "rjd3workspace")
mb_jws <- import_jws(file)
mb_jws
#> # A mable: 9 x 3
#> # Key:     sap, series [9]
#>   sap            series                                 sa
#>   <chr>          <chr>                             <model>
#> 1 SAProcessing-1 RF0812   <X-13ARIMA, ARIMA(2,1,1)(0,1,1)>
#> 2 SAProcessing-1 RF0893   <X-13ARIMA, ARIMA(0,1,1)(0,1,1)>
#> 3 SAProcessing-1 RF0899   <X-13ARIMA, ARIMA(0,1,1)(0,1,1)>
#> 4 SAProcessing-1 RF1011   <X-13ARIMA, ARIMA(2,1,0)(0,1,1)>
#> 5 SAProcessing-1 RF1012   <X-13ARIMA, ARIMA(1,1,1)(0,1,1)>
#> 6 SAProcessing-2 RF0893 <TRAMO-SEATS, ARIMA(1,1,1)(0,1,1)>
#> 7 SAProcessing-2 RF0899 <TRAMO-SEATS, ARIMA(0,1,1)(0,1,1)>
#> 8 SAProcessing-2 RF1011   <X-13ARIMA, ARIMA(0,1,2)(0,1,1)>
#> 9 SAProcessing-2 RF1012 <TRAMO-SEATS, ARIMA(1,1,1)(0,1,1)>

export_jws() does the opposite: it writes a new workspace, readable by the JDemetra+ graphical interface, from a mable of models. A workspace has a single context, so regressors of different series that have the same name but different values are renamed <name>_<sap>_<series>, in the context and in the specifications. Results, comments and links to data providers are not exported, and the series are stored as static data.

export_jws(mb_jws, tempfile(fileext = ".xml"))

Saving and reloading models

The Java object cannot be serialized: after saveRDS() / readRDS() (or when a model is created on a future worker) the Java pointer is no longer valid. fable.rjd3 handles this transparently: the data, the specifications and the context are stored as regular R objects, and the first time an extraction (components(), glance(), jd3_indicator(), forecast()…) is called on a reloaded model, the model is re-estimated. The following calls use the new Java object.

f <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")
saveRDS(mb, f)
mb_reloaded <- readRDS(f)

components(mb_reloaded)                 # the models are re-estimated here
#> # A dable: 288 x 7 [1M]
#> # Key:     .model [2]
#> # :        value = trend * seasonal * irregular
#>    .model    index value trend seasonal irregular season_adjust
#>    <chr>     <mth> <dbl> <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>         <dbl>
#>  1 x13    1949 Jan   112  122.    0.920     0.996          122.
#>  2 x13    1949 Feb   118  124.    0.948     1.00           125.
#>  3 x13    1949 Mar   132  126.    1.05      0.994          125.
#>  4 x13    1949 Apr   129  128.    1.00      1.01           129.
#>  5 x13    1949 May   121  128.    0.939     1.01           129.
#>  6 x13    1949 Jun   135  127.    1.07      0.998          127.
#>  7 x13    1949 Jul   148  126.    1.19      0.988          125.
#>  8 x13    1949 Aug   148  126.    1.17      0.999          126.
#>  9 x13    1949 Sep   136  127.    1.07      1.00           128.
#> 10 x13    1949 Oct   119  128.    0.925     1.00           129.
#> # ℹ 278 more rows
jd3_indicator(mb_reloaded, "sa")        # no new estimation
#> # A tibble: 288 × 4
#>    .model id       index value
#>    <chr>  <chr>    <mth> <dbl>
#>  1 x13    sa    1949 Jan  122.
#>  2 x13    sa    1949 Feb  125.
#>  3 x13    sa    1949 Mar  125.
#>  4 x13    sa    1949 Apr  129.
#>  5 x13    sa    1949 May  129.
#>  6 x13    sa    1949 Jun  127.
#>  7 x13    sa    1949 Jul  125.
#>  8 x13    sa    1949 Aug  126.
#>  9 x13    sa    1949 Sep  128.
#> 10 x13    sa    1949 Oct  129.
#> # ℹ 278 more rows

The estimation uses the versions of the rjd3* packages installed when the model is reloaded, which can differ from the versions used to fit it.

Limitations

  • Only yearmonth and yearquarter indices are supported, and the series must be univariate and regular. The interval between observations must divide a year, and a series with an interval of several months must start at the beginning of a period (for example in January or July for a semi-annual series).
  • The forecasts are those of the pre-adjustment model of the raw series; the components (trend, seasonal, irregular) are not forecasted.
  • The available indicator ids depend on the installed version of the rjd3* packages; use jd3_dictionary() to list them.
  • import_jws() only imports the SA-items estimated with an X-13ARIMA or a TRAMO-SEATS specification.
